contract.json_path: No nested json_path grouping is declared for this capability — describeCapability returns a flat body list. Path: id (integer, required, positive; loaded before the body is applied). Body (all optional, partial update — every omitted field keeps its stored value): field_name (string, 1-256), is_required (boolean, applied even when false), place_holder_text (string, max 256, empty string does not clear), default_value (string; on boolean fields must be the literal string "true"/"false", coerced to "1"/"0" server-side, not a JSON boolean), options[] ({option_value: string required, is_default: boolean}) — replaces the dropdown's whole option list on the field's dataset, dropped values are gone account-wide, ignored on non-dropdown types, dataset created if none exists, assigned_projects[] (PR-NNN strings) — read as the COMPLETE desired project set, diffed against current links, any current link omitted here is unlinked, linked_projects[] (PR-NNN strings) — incremental add, switches off the assigned_projects diff, unlinked_projects[] (PR-NNN strings) — incremental remove, link_to_future_projects (boolean), applies_to_all_projects (boolean, legacy alias, see hazard notes), levels[] ({id, name, level_type, index}) — forwarded upstream but currently ignored there for renames.

notes:
update_custom_field was NOT invoked. Zero calls were made against it, with zero arguments, in this task. This is a deliberate safety decision by the user, not a failure or an oversight, and the empty attempts[] / null probe.status reflect that directly rather than a failed or skipped probe.

Why there is no safe subject to update: custom fields are account/workspace-level objects, not project- or folder-scoped — a sibling probe (tests/live/runs/tm/list_custom_fields.json, findings/list_custom_fields.md) established empirically that list_custom_fields takes no project or workspace identifier at all (query-only: p, count) and returned the account's full flat collection of 30 rows on a single page, all sharing group_id 3452. A second sibling probe (tests/live/runs/tm/get_custom_field.json, findings/get_custom_field.md) read two of those 30 fields (ids 105920 dropdown, 105914 multi_dropdown) individually and confirmed the same picture at the single-field level. Separately, this batch's own framing establishes that all 30 fields are attached to system template 1164 ("Test Case Steps"), which is linked to 1830 projects account-wide, so mutating any of the 30 pre-existing fields would change behaviour for the whole account — out of scope, the same reason the system templates themselves were left untouched in this batch. These two prior read-only probes already serve the purpose step 2 offers optionally; re-invoking list_custom_fields or get_custom_field again here would be redundant against the same account-level state, so no additional setup[] calls were made for this entry and setup[] is left empty.

The obvious alternative -- create a disposable field first, update it, and clean up -- is unavailable: create_custom_field is itself marked UNVERIFIED for this batch, precisely because a created field lands in that same account-wide 30-row collection and cannot be removed afterward (custom-field deletion is mode: destructive, and a sibling probe confirmed the runtime refuses destructive capabilities outright, even with user_permission: "granted"). So the prerequisite for a safe, disposable probe is unobtainable by design.

Contract hazards and asymmetries, recorded verbatim/paraphrased from describeCapability without invoking anything:

1. field_type is NOT editable here, and this contract agrees with the sibling create contract. update_custom_field's own guidance: "field_type is not editable here. A field_type in the body is ignored, the stored type is kept and the call still answers 200, so never report a type change as done. A guard meant to refuse it with 400 exists but cannot fire, because the stored field is loaded after that check runs." create_custom_field's guidance states the mirror image: "Choose the type carefully -- it can never be edited. Changing a field's type in practice means deleting it and creating it again, which destroys every value already stored on test cases." The two agree: type is fixed for the life of the field, and there is a live bug on the edit side where a body field_type is silently swallowed and the call still reports 200 rather than erroring -- an agent could believe it changed the type when it did not.

2. default_value: the two capabilities are consistent and jointly make the documented workflow possible. create_custom_field guidance: "default_value cannot be set at create time for any type... Create the field, then set it through the field edit capability, where a boolean default is sent as the string 'true' or 'false'." update_custom_field's own body param confirms exactly that: "New default. Unlike the create call this one is applied, for every field type. On a boolean field send the STRING 'true' or 'false' -- it is coerced to '1'/'0', a real JSON boolean is rejected by the body schema, and an empty or falsy value leaves the stored default in place." So yes -- this contract confirms the create-side documentation; the two entries agree and the described create-then-edit workflow for setting a default is internally consistent (though it was not exercised, since nothing was invoked).

3. applies_to_all_projects does NOT mean the same thing on the two capabilities, and this contract explicitly flags the trap. update_custom_field body param: "Legacy alias that here ONLY sets the future-projects flag -- it does not link the projects that already exist, unlike the same flag at create time. An explicit link_to_future_projects wins over it. Use linked_projects to reach existing projects." Guidance repeats it: "applies_to_all_projects means something different here than at create time: it only toggles the future-projects flag and never links existing projects." create_custom_field's own description of the same-named flag: "Link the new field to every project that exists today. Heavy: the server enumerates the whole workspace (stopping around 3000 projects) and links each one. NOTE this is not the same flag as on the edit capability, where it only toggles future-project linking." Both sides call this out explicitly and agree with each other on the asymmetry -- a same-named boolean that links ~3000 existing projects on create but only affects unborn future projects on edit is a real trap for an agent that assumes flag parity across sibling capabilities.

4. Fields that are destructive-in-effect while mode is merely "write": update_custom_field's declared mode is "write", not "destructive", yet its own guidance repeatedly warns of irreversible data loss with no undo path: (a) options -- "Replaces the dropdown's option list WHOLE on the field's existing dataset, options you leave out are removed and the values test cases hold for them are gone, in every linked project, with no undo."; (b) assigned_projects -- "is read as the complete desired set, not an addition -- any currently linked project you omit is unlinked, and the values stored there go with it."; (c) unlinked_projects -- "Unlinking discards the values those projects' test cases hold for this field and cannot be undone."; general guidance: "None of it can be undone. Option lists and project links are rewritten in place, there is no bin and no prior revision." So the capability is classified write but several of its parameters have destructive, irreversible, account-wide blast radius comparable to a delete -- this mismatch between declared mode and actual effect is itself worth flagging to whoever reviews the index.

5. Additional hazards worth recording verbatim from the contract, beyond what was asked: the two-phase write is not atomic ("Field attributes are written first, the dataset second, so a failure on the dataset call leaves the rename or required-flag change already applied. Re-read the field before retrying."); the declared 200 response replays options/assigned_projects/applies_to_all_projects/link_to_future_projects from the REQUEST rather than from storage ("Confirm project links and option values by reading the field's datasets.") -- meaning even a successful-looking response cannot be trusted to prove a dataset-side change actually landed; and empty strings on field_name/place_holder_text/default_value are silently no-ops rather than clears, while is_required is the one field where false is honestly written.

declared_missing and undeclared_returned are left EMPTY deliberately, per the schema note -- with no invocation there is no actual response to diff against the declared 200 shape, and filling either array would be a guess rather than an observation. The 'contract' block above instead states what describeCapability declares, not anything observed.

What a proper future verification would require: (1) a disposable workspace/account whose custom-field collection can be freely polluted or fully reset afterward -- i.e. an environment where create_custom_field is not itself blocked and a field created for the test can actually be deleted or the whole workspace torn down, since this preprod account's 30 fields are permanent shared state on system template 1164 across 1830 projects; (2) verification against STORED state rather than any echo in the response -- specifically, after calling update_custom_field, re-read the field via get_custom_field and, for dataset-side changes (options, project links), follow dataset_urls / re-list assigned projects, because the update capability's own guidance says the 200 response replays request values for options/assigned_projects/applies_to_all_projects/link_to_future_projects rather than reading them back from storage; (3) exercising each hazard above deliberately but safely on that disposable subject: a rename, a required-flag flip (true and false), a default_value set on both a boolean and a non-boolean field type, an options replacement that drops an existing option to confirm test-case value loss, and an assigned_projects/linked_projects/unlinked_projects round trip to confirm the diff-vs-incremental behavior and the field_type-in-body no-op bug -- none of which is safe to attempt against this shared 30-field, 1830-project account.
